summary: T3-05 passes on the evidence I saw. All three story checks exit 0, with 121 tests passing. Each acceptance criterion is met in the implementation and has tests that exercise it. The diff touches only terrain.py and test_terrain_fingerprint.py, plus Ralph orchestration files (prd.json, progress.txt, ralph.sh, the agent log). There are no config/run.yaml changes, no mock data and no missing-evidence-as-zero. The remaining items are low-severity: the 3-cell and quarter-window rules are constants rather than config keys, and an exactly-representable plane gives texture H Unavailable with no resolution floor. Both are flagged as human decisions in the notes.

findings.claim: The 3-cell and quarter-window rules are hard-coded constants, not config keys.
findings.evidence: MIN_LAG_CELLS = 3.0 and MAX_LAG_WINDOW_FRACTION = 0.25. The story only requires these values and the notes flag the choice for a human, so this is acceptable.

resolution.reason: The three-cell and quarter-window rules are fixed PRD 6.3 rules ("Lags: at least three analysis cells and at most a quarter of the window width"), not tunable values. The PRD 8.13 config skeleton, which lists every terrain key, has only analysis_grid_m, lags_m, min_lags_for_H, min_lag_span_factor, detrend, min_valid_fraction and resampler. The tunable parts are read from config: lags_m and the window width. Adding a min_lag_cells or max_lag_window_fraction key would mean inventing config keys outside PRD 8.13, and it would require editing config/run.yaml, which is not in this story files list. The constants are named, documented with their PRD source (terrain.py:201-204), and boundary-tested at exactly 3 cells and exactly W/4. Decision (3) in the story notes flags a possible PRD 8.13 amendment for a human. The reviewer also rated this acceptable.

findings.claim: There is no resolution floor for texture nu. An exactly representable plane yields texture nu exactly 0 and nu_zero, while a plane given as rounded floats gives a tiny positive nu and an H fitted on rounding noise.
findings.evidence: Notes decision (5) records this for a human. The criteria forbid an epsilon, so it is not a defect.

resolution.reason: Adding a floor would break the acceptance criterion "No epsilon is added; log(0) is never evaluated" and the PRD 7 validity rule against epsilons. It would also be a new threshold that appears in neither PRD 6.3 nor the 8.13 config, while PRD 6.3 says terrain defaults change only on development data with a recorded reason. The behaviour is exact and deterministic: an exactly coplanar window gives texture nu = 0 and H Unavailable (nu_zero), and a non-coplanar window gives its true positive residual nu. PRD 7 (Tolerances) says real-data tolerances come from the product, so any vertical-precision floor belongs to product qualification of real DEMs on development data, not to this function. Decision (5) in the story notes records the option for a human. The reviewer also judged it not a defect.
